title: The Player
imageAlt: Abandoned hospital where the Player wakes up
summary: The human protagonist who wakes from a coma inside the abandoned hospital.
intro: The Player is the point-of-view character in Omni. They begin with no clear memory of the world's collapse and must judge whether the people they meet are safe, human, or only pretending.
facts: The Player wakes alone with no cell service and no staff nearby.
Their lack of context makes Ali's help feel necessary.
The Player was preserved, selected, or protected by Omni for reasons uncovered later in the story.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Player begins in a hospital bed after an unknown period of unconsciousness. The hospital is quiet, the town outside is empty, and no normal emergency systems respond.
The Player's early decisions are practical rather than heroic. They search for exits, supplies, signal, and other people because the world gives them no explanation.
As the story progresses, the Player becomes the test case for trust. Ali, Amy, and The Camp all offer safety while withholding information.
items: Role: human perspective in an almost-human world.
Opening objective: leave the hospital and find help.
Long-term objective: learn what happened and decide who deserves trust.

sections.heading: Known History
paragraphs: The Player was hospitalized before the game begins. The coma connects directly to the hospital records and becomes one of the first major personal reveals.
The Player was not simply forgotten. Their file, room, and treatment connect directly to Omni.
The Player does not know this early. Their confusion defines the opening tone.
items: Clue: medical charts that do not match normal coma care.
Clue: staff notes that refer to observation rather than recovery.
Reveal thread: other patients like the Player vanished before the opening.
